chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far al-Kumaydani narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hussein ibn Mus'ab al-Hamdani, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

Three things for which no one has an excuse: returning the trust to the good-doer and the wicked man, fulfilling the promise to the good-doer and the wicked man, and treating parents kindly whether they are good-doers or wicked ones.
ai.seo_question: What are the three actions for which there is no excuse regarding the moral status of the recipient?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three duties as universally binding, emphasizing that the moral status of the recipient does not exempt the giver from obligation. This underscores the Shia principle of *istiqra'* (consistency) in social ethics, where one maintains integrity in trusts, covenants, and filial piety regardless of whether the other party is righteous (*al-bar*) or wicked (*al-fajir*).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-118 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja’far ibn Abi Ja’far al-Kumaydany quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr that Al-Hussein ibn Mus’ab al-Hamedany heard As-Sadiq (MGB) say,

“There are three things that no one has any excuses not to do. Return what you are entrusted with whether it belongs to a good-doer or a wicked man. Fulfill your promise whether it be to a good-doer or a wicked man. Treat your parents kindly whether they are good-doers or wicked ones.”
